title: Queue pause summary: mark a summary as shortened when the read bound falls just after a space or tab
outcome: From the w-b63e1af0ce4c R13-1 review (Claude, delegation-92567411, Note at src/queue_pause_reason.rs:160). The summary reads at most one character past its 120-character bound. When the failure's first line is longer than that and the last character read is a space or tab, every word read is judged whole and plain. So redact_rest stays false, and the rest of the line is dropped with no "[redacted]" marker and no "...". Nothing leaks, because the unread part is never shown. But a reader may take the summary for the whole line, while the doc says the rest of the line is replaced with [redacted]. Fix direction: mark the summary as shortened (redact_rest or the ellipsis) whenever the line continues past what was read. Also, as cleanup in the same area: the restore of prior_pause_reason in the runtime-exit else branch (turn_lifecycle.rs, about line 2358) is a no-op and could be removed (Claude, same review).
acceptance: When a failure's first line continues past what queue_pause_summary reads, the summary always ends in a truncation or redaction marker, including when the last character read is a space or tab; an exact-output test covers that case.
